blocks: A raga carries characteristic phrases, ascent and descent rules, emphasized notes and a time of day on top of its pitches, so two ragas can share every pitch and still differ. A scale page records only the pitches and their names.
A raga has a page of its own

V. N. Bhatkhande grouped Hindustani ragas under ten parent scales, or thaats, in the early . A thaat is a pitch collection, so each thaat gets a scale page, as Music/Scale/Marwa and Music/Scale/Todi do, and a raga page links to the scale page of its parent thaat.

— codekiln and set up Logseq/Entity/Music/Scale with the naming rules this page explains, wrote a scale page for each entry in the scale menus of the MicroFreak user guide and the Launchpad Pro user guide, and linked each menu entry to its scale page.
The pitches of a Logseq/Entity/Music/Scale instance, as semitones above the tonic in twelve-tone equal temperament, in ascending order.
Space-separated integers from 0 to 11, starting with 0. For example, scale-semitones-above-tonic:: 0 2 4 5 7 9 11 on Music/Scale/Major.
A scale with different ascending and descending forms records the ascending form. The page body describes the other.
A name that sources spell in several ways records the most common form. The page body lists the variants.
A scale from a tradition that does not use equal temperament records the nearest equal-tempered pitches.
In this garden, Musical Work pages model identifiable compositions, songs, and separately named movements or other parts of a larger composition.
A musical work is an abstract composition or song, independent of any one performance, recording, or release.
A movement may have its own page when it is useful to track or discuss it separately. It remains related to its larger work through part-of::.
An album is a release or collection of recordings, not a musical work. Model an album under Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording and connect its tracks to their works.
An arrangement with a distinct identity may have its own work page, with based-on:: linking to the source work.

Place a work under its primary credited as <Identity>/Music/Work/<Title> when Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities is present. Without a separate credited identity, use Person/<Creator>/Music/Work/<Title>. A recording artist credit alone does not establish authorship of the underlying composition.
For a movement, continue below its parent work with a two-digit position and the movement's title, such as .../01 Grave - Allegro di molto e con brio.
Use the creator who gives the work its clearest home in the garden; list every creator whose page exists in created-by::.
Use the work's familiar title as the H1. Keep punctuation and diacritics from the established title.

Write a sharp or flat in a key as -sharp or -flat in both the page name and the H1, as Prelude in C-sharp Minor and Elegie in E-flat Minor. In Logseq # starts a tag, and ♯ and ♭ are hard to type into a link.
Use part-of:: on a movement or section page to link to its parent work.
Use appears-on:: on a work page to link to a known album recording or release. The album page lists its tracks in order as bullets, linking each work.
Use based-on:: for an adaptation or arrangement and cover-of:: on a cover recording to link the covered work.
A work page may link to performances and recordings, but those entities do not replace the work page.
Use music-form:: to link the Logseq/Entity/Music/Form pages a work belongs to, as music-form:: [[Music/Form/Prelude]].
Person/Madonna/Music/Work/Vogue is the song; Person/Madonna/Music/Recording/I'm Breathless is its album, whose ordered track list links to .
Person/Ludwig van Beethoven/Music/Work/Piano Sonata No. 8 in C Minor Op. 13 Pathétique/01 Grave - Allegro di molto e con brio is the first movement, nested beneath the sonata.
Person/John Cage/Music/Work/4'33" is a complete work with no movement pages required.
Person/Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart/Music/Work/Piano Concerto No. 23 in A Major K. 488/02 Adagio and .../03 Allegro assai are sibling movements under one concerto.
Person/Stevie Nicks/Music/Work/Landslide is the song. A Smashing Pumpkins recording of it is filed under that performer and links to the Stevie Nicks work with cover-of::.
Start each work page with logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Music/Work]] and one H1 containing the work's familiar title.
Add created-by:: links when the creator pages exist, and date-created:: when a reliable composition or publication date is known.
Add only relationships that are known and useful; leave unknown movement lists and release associations unstated.

Links a Logseq/Entity/Music/Work to the Logseq/Entity/Music/Form pages it belongs to.

In this garden, Synth Preset pages model saved synthesizer sounds and the evidence needed to describe or restore them.

A saved sound includes the settings and sequences stored by its instrument. A device slot is its current location. Stable page titles preserve links from composition and performance logs when metadata changes.

The name appears once in the filename and once in its instrument-specific name property. The body starts with - # Notes and holds listening observations, performance notes and links to music logs. Empty notes remain a heading without generated descriptions.

Sync owns documented device metadata in frontmatter and preserves handwritten body content. Sound descriptions require listening or verified parameters; a category and name cannot establish a signal chain.
An instance’s logseq-entity:: links to its data definition, using the narrowest known type such as Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak. Shared properties follow Logseq/Frontmatter.

Keys start with the owning type’s lowercase, hyphen-separated path: Preset/Synth gives preset-synth-; Preset/Synth/Microfreak gives preset-synth-microfreak-. Each property is documented under its owner’s Frontmatter/<literal-key> page as a Logseq/Entity/Frontmatter/Definition.

Each property definition has the literal key as an alias, connecting the clickable property name to its namespaced dictionary. Logseq Properties describes property pages; Logseq aliases describes alias references. Existing standalone pages with the same key need reconciliation before adding an alias.

Categorical values are explicit links to the definition’s child value pages; numeric and Boolean values retain their scalar types. A linked instrument model can supply an existing categorical vocabulary.
Numbered collections use and for adjacent populated slots. A page absent from the device has neither navigation property.

Human-readable properties describe verified parameters. Exact exports preserve data that may still lack a decoded dictionary. A complete reconstruction also needs referenced samples or wavetables, applicable global settings and the firmware context.

New parameter definitions state the source encoding, units, range, enum values and conversion, including raw values when a display conversion loses precision. Unknown parameters remain absent. A file digest identifies the exported bytes; it does not establish that every parameter has been decoded.
A Markdown link or URL to an exported preset file whose destination has been checked. Omit while no export is available.
The file preserves the format produced by its exporter. Restoration confidence requires the matching instrument, firmware and any separately stored sample or wavetable dependencies.
The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 computed over the exact bytes linked by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Frontmatter/preset-synth-file. Omit until the file exists.
A digest detects changes to that file. Equivalent sounds can have different export bytes, so a digest does not prove musical equivalence.
The established provenance of a saved sound. A slot number or name alone cannot establish provenance.
A sound established as user-created or modified from another sound.
A sound verified against an identified factory release or export.
The sound’s provenance has not been established.
In this garden, MicroFreak Synth Preset pages model individual saved sounds on the Microfreak, following Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth.

Pages use Microfreak/Preset/<slot> <name>, with a three-digit slot and the name observed at creation. The filename remains stable so existing music-log links resolve. A newly observed name at an occupied slot needs a new page when continuity is unknown.

Microfreak/Preset/396 Anit and Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit illustrate the frontmatter and notes format. Repeated names or slot numbers alone cannot establish that two observations are the same saved sound.
Shared provenance and export properties are defined by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth. Unknown origin uses Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Frontmatter/preset-synth-origin/Unknown.

The saved-header inventory reads slot, name, category and initialization status. It cannot detect a same-name edit to oscillator, filter, envelope, modulation or sequence settings. The Elektroid header decoder supplies the protocol evidence.

Elektroid’s preset download and serialization retain the preset payload for export: up to 146 blocks of 32 bytes. Supported payloads contain labeled raw parameter records for oscillator, filter, envelopes, LFO, modulation routes and preset settings. Repeated live reads matched the corresponding MIDI Control Center export byte for byte; the parameter inspection documentation records the framing and remaining interpretation limits.

The parameter inspection task reads a saved export with mise run microfreak:inspect /private/path/preset.bin or a computer project with mise run microfreak:inspect /private/path/project.mfprojz --slot 1. It reports exact stored bytes and named raw fields, identifies unsupported layouts, and leaves the input unchanged. Its preserves the distinction between raw values and unverified display conversions.

--interpret-fw5 adds the existing firmware 5 interpretations beside the raw fields: supported oscillator model and control names, normalized or metadata-scaled value domains, and source evidence for each interpretation. The report states the firmware assumption; an export does not establish its firmware version. Unknown models retain generic field names, and unsupported values retain their raw readings. The option leaves the raw report and preset notes intact.

Raw values describe saved base settings; modulation, performance gestures and unsaved edits affect the audible sound. Instrument display units, sequence contents, matrix destination meanings and referenced sample or wavetable identities require further verification. Firmware 5 oscillator indices follow the research cited in the optional interpretation report. A computer project can differ from the current device inventory.

Microfreak/UG/17 Ext Gear/09 MIDI CC Control and Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values describe MIDI control changes. A stream of knob movements is incomplete evidence of a saved sound: parameters that never change remain unobserved. Microfreak/UG/04 Presets/05 Digital Control explains why panel positions may differ from recalled values.

Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types defines oscillator models. Microfreak/UG/04 Presets/03 Preset Config defines per-preset settings, including voice behavior, scale and sequencer options. These guides describe meanings and ranges; values for a particular saved sound need a read or observation of that sound.

Samples and user wavetables have separate export workflows in Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/03 Samples Tab/01 Management and Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/02 Wavetables Tab/01 Management. A preset export alone does not establish that those resources are preserved. Global settings such as tuning and tempo behavior also affect playback; see Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/01 Device Tab.

A saved preset referenced by a published session has notes covering Saved export and provenance, Oscillator, Filter, Envelopes, LFO, Modulation matrix, and Performance and session context. These sections explain supported settings and their control meanings, with cited sources and explicit uncertainty.

Provenance identifies the export, capture date, bank or slot when relevant, and file digest. A verified match to an archived factory payload establishes that saved baseline; it does not establish a session-time capture or the instrument's unsaved state.

Values carry verified units or a clearly named normalized or raw domain. Unknown display conversions, matrix destinations, firmware assumptions and resource identities remain qualified. Large raw inventories stay outside the notes unless their numbers help explain the sound.

Performance notes distinguish what the saved patch supports from changes heard or recorded during a session. An unidentified initialized sound is described plainly rather than assigned an invented numbered preset or presumed settings.
The MicroFreak sync task previews the connected device with mise run microfreak:sync; --apply updates its saved metadata. The sync implementation on GitHub is also available as a .

--save-inventory /tmp/microfreak-inventory.json stores a full inventory; --inventory /tmp/microfreak-inventory.json previews that capture. --garden /absolute/path/to/worktree selects the destination and --port 'Arturia MicroFreak' selects an exact endpoint.

A complete successful inventory updates reported fields, omits initialized slots and marks missing sounds absent. Partial reads write nothing. Handwritten notes, established origin, verified oscillator type and export references survive metadata refreshes. A saved inventory describes its capture time; a new device read is needed to establish current state.
Header sync performs no binary export. File and digest properties are populated only after an export and its destination have been verified.
The category reported in the saved preset header, represented by one of the value pages below. The category labels the sound for browsing; the oscillator engine has its own property.
Elektroid’s category decoder maps the raw category byte to these names. Unknown codes must be reported before importing; their meaning cannot be inferred.

Page-link autocomplete under Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak/Frontmatter/preset-synth-microfreak-category/ lists the category pages. Logseq Properties explains property names, value autocomplete and page references.
Boolean true or false: the initialization bit in the last saved header. Initialized slots are omitted from the populated preset inventory.
The decoded bit is header[3] & 0x08; see Elektroid preset download.
The saved name returned by the device header, preserved as text. The current importer accepts 1–14 ASCII characters from its documented filename-safe alphabet and rejects unsupported names.
This property is the single occurrence of the preset name in page content. The filename carries the name used when the page was first created.
Integer from 1 to 512: the last observed device slot. A moved sound can retain its page title while this value changes.
The slot locates a saved sound; a slot alone cannot establish the identity of its contents.
Boolean true or false: whether this saved preset matched a populated slot in the latest successful full inventory.
A failed or partial inventory cannot establish absence. false retains the historical page and its notes; adjacent-slot navigation is removed.
A verified oscillator model page under Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types. The linked guide section defines the engine and the meanings of its Wave, Timbre and Shape controls.
This field is omitted until a saved value has been verified. The saved-header inventory supplies no oscillator type; a category such as Keys cannot determine the engine.
A manual observation must identify the saved preset being observed. The sync preserves this field but a change to other sound parameters requires a fresh verification.

In this garden, Question pages model a question I had at a particular time — one of the most frequent entities here. Typically Questions are stored under a topic namespace with a dedicated /Q/ segment so they stay findable and deduplicable.
Pages on disk match pages/*___Q___*.md (e.g. → mise___Q___How do I remove a mise tool%3F.md).
In-graph titles use a slash path such as Topic/Q/Question text or Topic/SubTopic/Q/Question text.
When we treat something as a question entity
Strong signals: the page captures a single answerable question; the title uses a topic namespace plus a fixed Q segment before the question wording; the body holds an answer (human, AI, or both).
When we treat something as a question entity
Not a question entity: general notes without the /Q/ naming convention, dashboards, CLI command stubs, or long-running threads better modeled as non-Q pages.
When we treat something as a question entity
Link shape: [[Topic/Q/Question text]] or [[Topic/SubTopic/Q/Question text]] as needed.
File shape: pages/Topic___Q___Question text.md with triple underscores between namespace parts; encode ? as %3F in the filename when present.
Use forward slashes in journal and body links; never triple underscores inside Logseq links.
Treat every new question as a question-entity candidate.
Practical search order for this type:
1. Exact expected page title / filepath under the topic namespace.
Practical search order for this type:
2. Grep normalized question text and key phrases across pages/**___Q___*.md.
Practical search order for this type:
Practical search order for this type:
4. H1 and first blocks on candidate pages; allow for minor rephrasing.
Practical search order for this type:
Classify each candidate as: existing, similar (needs human judgment), new, or blocked (missing config or ambiguous topic).
existing — the garden already holds the question. It gains an answer, not a second page.
Classify each candidate as: existing, similar (needs human judgment), new, or blocked (missing config or ambiguous topic).
similar — present the candidates and let a human decide before a near-duplicate lands.
Classify each candidate as: existing, similar (needs human judgment), new, or blocked (missing config or ambiguous topic).
On new question pages, include logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Question]] so this type page indexes instances.

Card-backed questions: when the H1 carries [[card]] and the page is a first-class review target, add a second entity marker: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Question]], [[Logseq/Entity/Card]] (see ). Card-backed questions use the compact page shape — see Card-backed page shape under Page shape below.

see-also:: — optional; extremely parsimonious list of 1-2 not obvious garden pages that are the best adjacent reading (strongest tie first). Do not put anything obvious in this list, do not restate parent-namespace context the title already encodes. Do not use see-also:: for external URLs (put those in the answer body).
via:: — optional; only for what logseq page best represents the context in which the question appeared - only useful when astonishing; be parsimonious and only use this when it's not obvious.
tags:: / alias:: — only when they match established patterns on sibling question pages in the same topic; never alter existing tags:: on a page you did not create for tagging migration.
Shared frontmatter conventions live on Logseq/Frontmatter.
H1 — the question text; link key terms to existing pages where it helps.
Optional inline [[card]] at the end of the H1 — only when the human operator explicitly requests it. Do not add [[card]] speculatively, even if the question seems like good SRS material.
## [[My Answer]] — optional; / working answer (steps, tables, [[tldr]], verified command examples).
## [[My Notes]] — optional; do not create by default. Tangents and links that are not the direct answer.
## [[AI Answer]] — standard heading for AI-researched answers. Answer content is direct children of this block; do not add a [[AI/Response]] child wrapper.
[[Answer/Official]] (alias [[Official Answer]]) — used when the answer is from official documentation; include a markdown link inline: [[Answer/Official]] from [Source Title](url).
## [[AI Answer]] — standard heading for AI-researched answers. Answer content is direct children of this block; do not add a [[AI/Response]] child wrapper.
Lead with Short answer: when useful.
## [[AI Answer]] — standard heading for AI-researched answers. Answer content is direct children of this block; do not add a [[AI/Response]] child wrapper.
Cite external docs with markdown links in the answer body.
## [[AI Answer]] — standard heading for AI-researched answers. Answer content is direct children of this block; do not add a [[AI/Response]] child wrapper.
Bold for labels; backticks for commands. Do not wrap `commands` in **…** (see ).
## [[AI Answer]] — standard heading for AI-researched answers. Answer content is direct children of this block; do not add a [[AI/Response]] child wrapper.
Do not add ## Related solely to list internal wikilinks; use see-also:: instead.

When logseq-entity:: includes and the H1 ends with [[card]], omit the ## Answer section header and attribution block. The answer sits directly as a child bullet of the H1, as short as a card prompt requires:
Use ==highlight== to mark mnemonic cues in the answer (e.g. ==N==ext Window).
Wikilink key terms in both the question and the answer to existing entity pages.

Choose the topic namespace first. It is the domain or tool the question is about — Claude Code, git, LangSmith, EdTech/Idea/LearnMark. Infer it from the question when the human did not name one; ask rather than guess when nothing plausible presents itself.
Keep the question's full wording, punctuation included, as the page title. Normalize trailing ? for searching only.
The filing is recorded in today's journal like any other graph edit — a new page under [[Filed]], an edited one under [[Updated]], per .
Commit the drafted question page and its journal entry by default, unless the human asks to leave them uncommitted.
Filing and answering are one pass: once the page and its journal line exist, research the answer rather than leaving a bare question.
Draw on whatever is at hand — the garden's own pages first, then official documentation, then web search. Prefer a source that can be cited over recollection.
Write the answer into ## [[AI Answer]] per Page shape above, marking it [[Answer/Official]] when it comes from official docs.
When the answer cannot be settled, say so on the page and tell the human what is missing. An honestly open question is worth more than a confident wrong one.
Card: [[card]] on the H1 plus [[Logseq/Entity/Card]] in frontmatter when the question page itself is reviewable; distinct from factoring a prompt into a /Card/ namespace page under .
CLI commands / flags: questions about commands link to and instances; they are not substitutes for command reference stubs.
Older ___Q___ pages may lack logseq-entity::, use ## Related for internal links (use see-also:: instead), or use ## [[AI/Response]] as the section heading instead of the correct form.
Do not bulk-migrate unless requested; new pages should follow the rules above.
In this garden, Series pages model an ordered sequence of another entity type — a named run of works that should cluster together, and appear in intended order, when paths are sorted .
Series is not a standalone kind of work. A page that belongs to a sequence declares both types, primary entity first: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Book]], [[Logseq/Entity/Series]].
The hub that names the sequence may declare Series alone, or Series plus the member type when the sequence is also treated as one work.
Any entity type that has ordered installments can combine with Series: books, podcast episodes, talks, courses, essay runs, software version lines, and others.
Naming — Series after the member type
By default the Series segment sits after the member type and before the instance: …/<Type>/Series/<Series Name>/….
Naming — Series after the member type
Members then share that prefix, so they cluster under the series on disk.
Naming — Series after the member type
